name: What is the difference between an alcove tub and a freestanding tub?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an alcove tub and a freestanding tub?

acceptedAnswer.text: An alcove tub fits into a three-wall enclosure and is typically paired with tile or a wall surround, making it the most space-efficient choice for standard layouts. A freestanding tub stands alone, serving as a decorative focal point, but it requires significantly more open floor space and clear access around all sides for cleaning. Freestanding tubs often demand relocated water supply and drain lines rough-in through the floor, whereas alcove tubs usually connect directly to existing wall plumbing. If your bathroom has compact square footage, an alcove tub preserves usable room while keeping framing simple.
acceptedAnswer.description: Alcove tubs fit between three walls to maximize floor space, while freestanding tubs require a larger room, open floor clearance, and specialized rough-in plumbing.
